title: hello-optimize — the smallest proof of active eval optimization (target: cli)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: “The smallest possible demonstration of Pillar 2 — active eval optimization.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — the eval and the optimizer both call the model.

groups.title: Beat 1 · A prompt that is deliberately too terse

beats.label: Say what it's for
beats.cue: “A CLI agent whose system prompt is deliberately short so the optimizer has room.”

beats.label: Document the run in the header
beats.cue: The header carries the optimize invocation — dataset, graders, iterations, seed. Its hello-optimize/ prefixes predate the self-contained-starter convention; we run it from right here.

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: target: cli — eval, optimize and flywheel only run against cli specs.

beats.label: The instruction the optimizer will rewrite
beats.cue: “Answer the user's question.” That terseness is the experiment, not a mistake.

beats.label: No tools at all
beats.cue: Nothing to blame but the prompt — which is exactly what we're tuning.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “lint: clean — no findings.” Parse, the IR passes, and the scope audit.

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “The spec is sugar; this JSON is what the compiler actually sees.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target cli

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: Shape asserted, deps installed, booted to the credentials gate: GREEN with no key.

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the credentials gate

beats.label: Open the emitted agent
beats.cue: The instructions ride into the bundle as a string — that string is the tuning target.

groups.title: Beat 3 · Run it, then measure it

beats.label: Ask it one question
beats.cue: [needs-key] One turn, and no guidance beyond “answer the user's question”.
beats.command: crewhaus run live/crewhaus.yaml --prompt "What is the capital of France?"

beats.label: Open the dataset
beats.cue: Ten capital-of-X questions, each with its expected output.

beats.label: Open the grader
beats.cue: One grader — type: contains, and substring: is a LITERAL. Read that line twice: it does not mean “the sample's expected_output”.

beats.label: Score the baseline
beats.cue: [needs-key] The baseline, measured before anything changes: pass_rate=0.0%, and every rationale reads `output missing "expected_output"`. The eval found the bug — and it's in the grader.
beats.command: crewhaus eval live/crewhaus.yaml --dataset dataset.jsonl --graders graders.yaml -o live/eval-before

verify.note: runs the agent over 10 samples; needs Anthropic credentials. Measured on CLI 0.4.0: pass_rate=0.0% mean_score=0.000 — `type: contains` searches the answer for the literal text "expected_output" (the grader that compares against the sample is `type: expected_contains`), so every sample fails even though every answer is correct

groups.title: One more thing · The patch is the artifact

beats.label: Run the optimizer
beats.cue: [needs-key] Five seeded iterations of the rule-based mutator, scored on the 70/30 dev split. “score: 0.000 → 0.000 (Δ +0.000)” — a grader nothing can satisfy gives the search no gradient.
beats.command: crewhaus optimize live/crewhaus.yaml --dataset dataset.jsonl --graders graders.yaml --iterations 5 --seed 42 -o live/optimize

verify.note: re-evals the dev split per candidate; needs Anthropic credentials. Measured on CLI 0.4.0: `[optimize] score: 0.000 → 0.000 (Δ +0.000)` then `no improvement above threshold 0.01; source untouched.` — every candidate ties at zero because of the graders.yaml defect the eval beat surfaced

beats.label: Open the patch it emitted
beats.cue: [needs-key] The patch is emitted either way — and this one is honest about itself: value is the original prompt, rationale “improved fitness by 0.000 over 5 iterations”.

verify.note: reads the patch.json the previous (needs-key) optimize beat writes into live/optimize/. Measured: {"path":["agent","instructions"],"op":"replace","value":"Answer the user's question.","rationale":"rule-based mutator improved fitness by 0.000 over 5 iterations"}

beats.label: Ask it to apply the winner
beats.cue: [needs-key] --write-back is a gate, not a rubber stamp: “no improvement above threshold 0.01; source untouched.” It will not edit your spec to say nothing.

verify.note: write-back is conditional — eval-optimizer-orchestrator/src/index.ts:338 writes only when `applied` (improvement ≥ the 0.01 threshold). At Δ 0.000 nothing is written, so this take ends on the refusal, not on an edit. Would mutate the scratch live/crewhaus.yaml, never the committed spec

beats.label: Diff it against the committed spec
beats.cue: [needs-key] Nothing. The optimizer declined to touch the spec — and the committed starter was never in the blast radius either way.

verify.note: measured: no output, exit 0 — live/crewhaus.yaml is still the byte-identical copy the spec beats typed. It would exit 1 with a diff if write-back had fired
